log: DOES A STRUCTURAL CHANGE PROPAGATE THROUGH CONNECTED SPHERES -- and does it carry the TRUTH?
Methylate a cytosine and let the consequence spread: what moves, how far, and what that moves
in turn. Energy was already shown not to stay inside a small sphere; STRUCTURE is a different
question, because displacement really does travel through contacts. So it gets its own run.
Ground truth is available -- the network is sparse, so the exact displacement field is solved
directly and every sphere scheme is graded against it, not against another model.
1KX5 without waters: 13625 atoms (6021 DNA). Ordered waters are dropped from
the MECHANICAL network deliberately -- they are not covalently held and would act as springs
transmitting stress they cannot actually transmit.
elastic network: 263765 springs within 6.0 A (covalent pairs under 1.8 A stiffened 20x)

READING
best relative error:  schwarz_true 9.476e-01   schwarz_local 9.789e-01   same tiling + CG 8.926e-08
THE TILING IS FINE. THE COMMUNICATION RULE IS WHAT DECIDES IT.
The SAME spheres reach the exact field to 8.9e-08 once each sphere is corrected
against a whole-structure residual. So sphere coverage genuinely can carry a structural
change -- the geometry was never the problem.
But spheres that see ONLY THEIR OWN ATOMS stop dead at 0.979 relative error and
STOP BECAUSE THEY HAVE CONVERGED, not because they ran out of sweeps. They settle onto
the exact solution of a network cut at every sphere boundary, and from inside the scheme
that is indistinguishable from success: the updates go to zero, everything looks done.
THAT IS THE FALSE INFORMATION. It is not noise in the answer, it is a confident answer
to a different question, and no amount of extra sweeps or smaller spheres repairs it.
What repairs it is one global pass per sweep -- which is the thing the scheme was meant
to avoid needing.
